questionText:
Which among the following statements are correct about elections in

(A) In the first general election, it was decided to place inside each polling
booth a box for each candidate with the election symbol of that candidate.
(B) After the first two elections, the polling method was changed. Now the
ballot paper carried the names and symbols of all the candidates and voter
was required to put a stamp on the name of the candidate they want to vote

(C) Towards the end of the 1990s, the Election Commission started using

(D) By 2004 the entire country had shifted to the EVM.
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text:
(B), (C) and (D) Only
Which among the following statements are correct about elections in
India?
 
(A) In the first general election, it was decided to place inside each polling
booth a box for each candidate with the election symbol of that candidate.
(B) After the first two elections, the polling method was changed. Now the
ballot paper carried the names and symbols of all the candidates and voter
was required to put a stamp on the name of the candidate they want to vote
for.
(C) Towards the end of the 1990s, the Election Commission started using
the EVM.
(D) By 2004 the entire country had shifted to the EVM.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Syllabus Core (Era of One-Party Dominance):
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 2: Era of One-Party Dominance, 'Changing Methods of Voting', p. 31 box): 'In the first general election, it was decided by the Election Commission to place inside each polling booth a ballot box for each candidate with the election symbol of that candidate. After the first two general elections, this method was changed. Now the ballot paper carried the names and symbols of all the candidates and the voter was required to put a stamp on the name of the candidate. Towards the end of the 1990s the Election Commission started using the EVM. By 2004 the entire country had shifted to the EVM.' All four statements (A), (B), (C), and (D) are verbatim correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 2: Era of One-Party Dominance, 'Changing Methods of Voting', p. 31 box): 'In the first general election, it was decided by the Election Commission to place inside each polling booth a ballot box for each candidate with the election symbol of that candidate.
